title: Keyboard Manager: Remapped Copilot key (F23) not recognized in Citrix Workspace session

status.label: Likely native Citrix ownership
status.detail: A separate third-party Copilot remapper fails in native Citrix in the same way, while the remap works locally and in Citrix HTML5.

next_action.label: Explain native Citrix ownership
next_action.reason: The new independent reproduction makes a PowerToys-only fix unlikely; preserve the evidence and direct further investigation to Citrix/native transport.

judgment.rationale: The latest discussion adds an independent third-party remapper reproduction: it works locally but is also ignored by native Citrix, and its author believes Citrix uses low-level input handling that cannot be intercepted. Together with the earlier native-versus-HTML5 split, this is stronger evidence of native Citrix transport or filtering than of a PowerToys Keyboard Manager defect.
evidence: PowerToys remapping works locally and in Citrix HTML5 but fails in native Citrix Workspace.
The third-party Copilot Key+ remapper also works locally and fails in native Citrix, according to the issue's latest comments.
The third-party author reports that their remapper may not be able to intercept the low-level native Citrix driver path.
The reporter already supplied the native Citrix version, Windows build, remap, TransparentKeyPassthrough behavior, and the HTML5 comparison.
Keyboard Manager's relevant injection path is local Windows input generation; no public evidence shows that PowerToys emits a malformed replacement stream before Citrix receives it.
judgment.recommended_action: Do not request another PowerToys diagnostic solely to reproduce the same cross-tool failure. Post a specific ownership clarification and leave any code change to a future trace that proves PowerToys emits an incorrect event sequence.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is not currently justified. The same native-Citrix failure occurs with an independent remapper, while the browser client accepts the remap; this points to native Citrix low-level input ownership rather than a PowerToys-only defect.

issue_context.summary: The Copilot/F23-to-Right-Ctrl remap works on Windows and in Citrix HTML5, but native Citrix ignores it; an independent remapper now reports the same native-Citrix failure.
known_information: The issue concerns a Win+Shift+F23 Copilot key remapped to Right Ctrl.
The reporter supplied PowerToys 0.96.1, Windows 11 build 26200.7171, Citrix Workspace 25.8.10.36, and the TransparentKeyPassthrough trade-off.
The remap works locally and in Citrix HTML5 through Edge but fails in native Citrix Workspace.
Setting TransparentKeyPassthrough to Local makes the remap work but prevents expected remote Alt+Tab behavior.
A third-party Copilot Key+ remapper was tested and shows the same local-success/native-Citrix-failure pattern.
The third-party author believes native Citrix uses low-level handling that their program cannot intercept.
The issue has Issue-Bug, Product-Keyboard Shortcut Manager, Product-Keyboard Manager, and Needs-Triage labels and no assignee.
inferences: The matching failure across two independent remappers makes native Citrix capture, filtering, or transport more likely than a PowerToys-specific modifier-ordering defect.
Citrix HTML5 succeeding suggests the browser event path is materially different from native Workspace input handling.
A PowerToys fix should not be proposed unless a native-Citrix trace first proves that Keyboard Manager emits an incorrect or incomplete replacement sequence.
issue_context.analysis: The newest comment supplies the previously missing comparative evidence without requiring another reporter capture: an unrelated remapper fails in the same native client while working locally. That directly weakens the prior red PowerToys event-order hypothesis and changes ownership assessment toward native Citrix. The existing workaround and supplied TransparentKeyPassthrough details also show that changing Citrix capture policy affects the result, but at an unacceptable shortcut-transport cost.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, all comments through 2026-09-07T18:39:04Z, labels, assignees, and author metadata.
Compared the native Citrix versus HTML5 behavior described by the reporter with the independent Copilot Key+ reproduction in the latest discussion.

Reviewed Keyboard Manager's local remapping flow in the repository, including HandleShortcutRemapEvent and the SetModifierKeyEvents/SetKeyEvent injection helpers; the public evidence does not establish a defect in that emitted local sequence.
Checked related remote-input history and issue context; the cross-client split is consistent with an external transport boundary, not a duplicate PowerToys implementation fix.

information_gaps.information: A future native-Citrix event trace proving that PowerToys emits an incorrect replacement sequence before Citrix filtering.
information_gaps.why_needed: Only this evidence would reopen a PowerToys code-fix path after the independent remapper comparison.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture local hook/injection events and the corresponding native Citrix remote result in the same reproduction; do not recollect the already supplied version, workaround, or HTML5 comparison.

comment.body: Thanks for testing Copilot Key+ as an independent comparison. The fact that both PowerToys and a separate remapper work locally but are ignored by native Citrix, while the HTML5 client accepts the remap, points to native Citrix's low-level keyboard capture or transport rather than a PowerToys-only mapping defect. The existing `TransparentKeyPassthrough=Local` result further shows that Citrix capture policy changes the behavior, but it also explains why that is not an acceptable general workaround because it breaks remote Alt+Tab. We do not have a justified PowerToys code change to propose unless a future trace shows that Keyboard Manager emits an incorrect replacement sequence before native Citrix handles it.
